items.title: After an etale base change a finite type algebra splits into a finite part and a part quasi-finite nowhere over the point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite type map and a prime of the base there is an etale neighbourhood over which the base change splits as a product of finite factors, each with a unique prime over the point, and a remainder that is quasi-finite nowhere over that point (statement lines 40578-40600). The proof does not work under a quasi-finiteness assumption: it analyses the fibre, splits off its finitely many isolated closed points, spreads them out to finite factors over an etale neighbourhood, and verifies the listed properties for the resulting decomposition (proof lines 40602-40635). Separating the isolated points of the fibre is the step that produces the finite factors. H2.
